results.controlling_authority_on_mismatch: TWO convergent residential routes, both independent of the commercial statute: (1) WAIVER - EDC Associates, Ltd. v. Gutierrez (1984) 153 Cal.App.3d 167 (residential; acceptance of rent after a 3-day notice creates an implied waiver of the notice; landlord bears the burden to prove it overcame the waiver, e.g., by returning the payment uncashed as in Highland Plastics, Inc. v. Enders (1980) 109 Cal.App.3d Supp. 1); CACI No. 4324 (Waiver by Acceptance of Rent). (2) OVERSTATEMENT / STRICT COMPLIANCE - CCP 1161(2) requires the notice to state the exact amount due; once $500 is accepted, the $2,000 demanded no longer matches the $1,500 remaining, so the notice is defective (Nourafchan v. Miner; Lynch & Freytag v. Cooper). CONTRAST: CCP 1161.1 is the COMMERCIAL statute and reaches the OPPOSITE result (1161.1(b): a commercial landlord may accept partial rent and proceed without re-serving, if it gave a reservation-of-rights/non-waiver notice); 1161.1(d) expressly excludes residential dwelling units. Do NOT apply 1161.1 to a residential fact pattern.
